### **Overview**

This is an assignment to read in 4 time series .csv files, and calculate the mean and standard deviation of both temperature and light intensity for each file (each tide pool), using both the `base-R for loop` function, and the `purrr map()` function.

### **Load Libraries**

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

### **Load Data**

List files in a directory first by pointing to the folder on the computer and specifying all files in that path that match a pattern.

```{r}
# List files in a directory
# Point to the folder on the computer
HomeworkPath <- here("Week_13", "Data", "homework")

# List all files in that path matching a pattern
# Saves the entire path with full.names so it works with read_csv()
files <- dir(path = HomeworkPath, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
files
```


### **Method 1: for loop**

#### Pre-allocate space for the loop

```{r}
# Pre-allocate space for the loop
# One row for each file and 5 columns
homework_data <- tibble(PoolID = rep(NA, length(files)),
                        mean_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                        sd_temp = rep(NA, length(files)),
                        mean_light = rep(NA, length(files)),
                        sd_light = rep(NA, length(files)))
homework_data
```

#### Test with the basic code first

```{r}
# Write the basic code first
# Test by reading in the first file
raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(files[1]))
head(raw_data)

# Calculating mean and standard deviation
mean_temp <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_temp<- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
c(mean_temp, sd_temp)
```

#### Turn it into a for loop

```{r}
# Turn it into a for loop
for (i in seq_along(files)) {
  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(files[i]))
  
  homework_data$PoolID[i] <- raw_data$PoolID[i]
  homework_data$mean_temp[i] <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  homework_data$sd_temp[i] <- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  homework_data$mean_light[i] <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
  homework_data$sd_light[i] <- sd(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
}
homework_data
```

### **Method 2: purrr map()**

```{r}
# Use map() to read in files
# Then stack lisk of dataframes into one with list_rbind()
# Calculate means and standard deviations with group_by() and summarise()
data <- files |> 
  set_names() |> 
  map(read_csv) |> 
  list_rbind(names_to = "filename") |> 
  group_by(PoolID) |> 
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_temp = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_light = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_light = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE))
data
```

### **Check if both outputs match exactly**

```{r}
identical(homework_data, data)
```
